LESSON: READING 1.2.1 READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension, part of Strand 1 in Grade 9 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How should you read for comprehension? 2. Why are community heroes and heroines important in the society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. explain the pre-reading steps to peers,

2. read a text on community heroes and heroines and make short notes,

3. identify vocabulary related to community heroes and heroines from the texts,

4. collaborate with peers to conduct a spelling-bee mini-contest to spell the vocabulary identified,

5. work jointly with peers to infer the meaning of vocabulary from context,

6. make notes on the main ideas from a text and share with peers,

7. make a summary of a section of the text,

8. share the summaries with their peers for review,

9. answer direct and inferential questions from the text. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. explain the pre-reading steps to peers,
2. read a text on community heroes and heroines and make short notes,
3. identify vocabulary related to community heroes and heroines from the texts,
4. collaborate with peers to conduct a spelling-bee mini-contest to spell the vocabulary identified,
5. work jointly with peers to infer the meaning of vocabulary from context,
6. make notes on the main ideas from a text and share with peers,
7. make a summary of a section of the text,
8. share the summaries with their peers for review,
9. answer direct and inferential questions from the text. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 1.2.1 Reading for Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem-solving: This is enhanced as the learner follows simple instructions during the spelling-bee

mini-contest to spell the vocabulary identified.

• Citizenship: It is promoted as the learner accumulates information when reading a text on community heroes and heroines

and makes short notes.

Values:
• Unity: It is promoted as the learner cooperates with peers to conduct a spelling-bee mini-contest to spell the vocabulary

identified.

• Love: The learner displays trustworthiness when sharing the summaries with their peers for review.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social Cohesion: The is promoted as the learner interacts with texts on community heroes and heroines.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of writing summaries to the learning of reading strategies in English.
